[ What could go wrong? ]

Five redesigns, same batter

What she wanted
  • A site that looked "more groomed, professional, and exciting"
  • Something she was proud to send clients to
What was actually missing
  • Clearly defined services
  • A primary goal for the site
  • One clear ideal client (she described four)
The result

If we'd jumped straight into fonts and colors, we'd have built a gorgeous site with the exact same problems as the old one. It’s frosting with no cake.

→

[ BUT WHAT ABOUT DIY? ]

DIY? Same ingredients,
different recipe

01 – The blank screen
  • Pick a platform
  • Pick colors and fonts
  • Open the first page
  • Stare at a blank screen
  • Close the laptop
02 – The almost-site
  • Friend takes pics, you write copy
  • Build for a weekend (or a month)
  • Doesn't match what you pictured
  • No new clients show up
  • Embarrassed to share the URL
  • Subscription isn't moving the needle
→

When you build on vibes

  • Services that aren't clearly defined
  • No obvious next step for visitors
  • Messaging that tries to speak to everyone (and lands with no one)
  • A user journey that's more of a meander than a path

You can redesign and tweak over and over – but without the foundational ingredients, you’ll keep pulling the same sunken cake out of the oven.

→

Why this happens
(and why it's totally normal)

  • You're running a business. You're busy serving clients and doing the work you're amazing at.
  • Nobody explains the real prep. Most resources jump straight to design tips or copy formulas.
  • The info is scattered. Blog posts, Google, a YouTube video you stumbled on. Hard to know what you actually need.

The 5-step website prep framework

01

Your Site's #1 Job

Define what it's hired to do

02

Your Ideal Audience

Know who you're talking to

03

Your Brand Bio

Say it like you mean it

04

Your Offers

Get specific on how to work with you

05

Your Proof

Round up the receipts

→

[ STEP 01 ]

01

Define your website goals

Identify one primary (and optionally one secondary) call to action. This guides every structure and design decision.

Why it matters

A website without clear goals is just a pretty business card.

→

[ STEP 02 ]

02

Clarify your ideal audience

You don't need a hyper-focused niche, but you do need to know who your site and services are for.

Why it matters

Knowing who your visitors are means you know what they need to see in order to work with you.

→

[ STEP 03 ]

03

Lock down your brand bio

Get clear on your 2–3 sentence bio that tells the world who you are, what you do, how you help.

Why it matters

If you can't introduce yourself clearly, your website can't either.

→

[ STEP 04 ]

04

Get your offers organized

Get specific on how people can work with you: process, logistics, deliverables.

Why it matters

Unclear service pages mean visitors leave without booking.

→

[ STEP 05 ]

05

Gather your social proof

Collect testimonials and results that address specific client concerns at each stage of their journey.

Why it matters

Strategic social proof converts hesitant visitors into clients.

→

[ What's Next? ]

Get it done

1

Allow 4–6 weeks (or one focused week)

Spread it out, or block dedicated time.

2

Reach out for missing content

Testimonials, photos, or quotes from past clients.

3

Build one organization tool

One folder, doc, or Notion page that holds everything.

DIY: build it yourself

From scratch, or from a pre-made template you customize yourself
Pros
  • Total control
  • Rock-bottom investment (still pretty low with a template)
  • A template gives you a professional design base – no staring at a blank page
Cons
  • The learning curve is steep steep (moderate with a template)
  • Will eat your time – likely the longest timeline to actually launch
  • Without a pro designer and copywriter, conversions will likely suffer
  • SEO is entirely on you
→

DWY: build it with a guide

The middle ground most people don't know exists (!)
Pros
  • Expert guidance without giving up control
  • You learn the why behind every decision, so you can manage and evolve your site long after launch
  • Moderate investment compared to fully DFY
Cons
  • You still need to show up and do the work – this isn't a hand-it-off situation
  • Timelines depend on the program structure, and you're the one making decisions (with support, but still you)
→

DFY: hire it out

A designer customizes a template for you, or builds from scratch
Pros
  • Professional, conversion-focused design that handles things you might not think of
  • Largely hands-off for you
  • Fast launch (semi-custom), or wide-open design options (fully custom)
Cons
  • Moderate to highest investment
  • Less control – you'll need to make quick decisions and trust the process
  • Wait times can be long depending on the designer's availability
